metadata.title: Hypertension Clinical Practice Guidance
metadata.author: Clinical Quality and Pharmacy & Therapeutics Committee

protocol.summary: This guidance covers blood pressure measurement, categories, treatment goals, medication titration, laboratory monitoring, and follow-up for adults with hypertension. It also describes escalation actions and care-management check-ins.

scope.population: Adults 18 years and older enrolled in Disease Management or the Special Needs Plan care program.
exclusions: Pregnancy or the first 12 weeks postpartum
Secondary hypertension managed by a specialist

thresholds.action: Reinforce healthy lifestyle; recheck yearly.
thresholds.source: Normal: systolic below 120 and diastolic below 80 mmHg. Reinforce healthy lifestyle; recheck yearly.

thresholds.label: Severe elevation
thresholds.action: Without symptoms, contact the treating provider the same day and recheck within 1 week. With listed symptoms, direct the patient to call 911 or go to the emergency department.
thresholds.source: Severe elevation: systolic 180 or higher, or diastolic 120 or higher.

thresholds.label: Severe elevation
thresholds.action: Without symptoms, contact the treating provider the same day and recheck within 1 week. With listed symptoms, direct the patient to call 911 or go to the emergency department.
thresholds.source: Severe elevation: systolic 180 or higher, or diastolic 120 or higher.

thresholds.label: Low BP
thresholds.action: Do not increase any antihypertensive; provider review within 1 business day.
thresholds.source: Low BP: systolic below 100 mmHg, or dizziness or fainting on standing. Do not increase any antihypertensive; provider review within 1 business day.

decisionRules.when: When blood pressure is Stage 1 and the 10-year ASCVD risk is 10% or higher, or the patient has diabetes or chronic kidney disease, then start medication.
decisionRules.source: Start medication when 10-year ASCVD risk is 10% or higher, or the patient has diabetes or chronic kidney disease.

decisionRules.when: When blood pressure is more than 20/10 mmHg above goal, then start two first-line agents from different classes.
decisionRules.then: Start two first-line agents from different classes.
decisionRules.source: When BP is more than 20/10 mmHg above goal, start two first-line agents from different classes.

decisionRules.when: When severe elevation occurs without symptoms, then contact the treating provider the same day and recheck within 1 week.
decisionRules.then: Contact the treating provider the same day; recheck within 1 week.
decisionRules.source: Without symptoms: contact the treating provider the same day; recheck within 1 week.

decisionRules.when: When severe elevation occurs with chest pain, shortness of breath, new weakness or numbness, confusion or vision change, then direct the patient to call 911 or go to the emergency department.
decisionRules.then: Direct the patient to call 911 or go to the emergency department.
decisionRules.source: With chest pain, shortness of breath, new weakness or numbness, confusion or vision change: direct the patient to call 911 or go to the emergency department.

decisionRules.when: When systolic blood pressure is below 100 mmHg, or there is dizziness or fainting on standing, then do not increase any antihypertensive and arrange provider review within 1 business day.
decisionRules.then: Do not increase any antihypertensive; provider review within 1 business day.
decisionRules.source: Low BP: systolic below 100 mmHg, or dizziness or fainting on standing. Do not increase any antihypertensive; provider review within 1 business day.

decisionRules.when: When potassium is above 5.5 mmol/L, or creatinine is up more than 30% from baseline, then hold the new or increased agent, repeat the panel within 72 hours and notify the provider.
decisionRules.then: Hold the new or increased agent, repeat the panel within 72 hours and notify the provider.
decisionRules.source: Potassium above 5.5 mmol/L, or creatinine up more than 30% from baseline: hold the new or increased agent, repeat the panel within 72 hours and notify the provider.

decisionRules.when: When potassium is below 3.5 mmol/L on a thiazide-type diuretic, then notify the provider for replacement.
decisionRules.source: Potassium below 3.5 mmol/L on a thiazide-type diuretic: notify the provider for replacement.

decisionRules.when: When proportion of days covered is below 80%, then refer to a pharmacist.
decisionRules.source: Proportion of days covered below 80% triggers a pharmacist referral.

decisionRules.when: When two consecutive check-ins show average home systolic BP 10 mmHg or more above goal despite confirmed adherence, then obtain provider review within 5 business days.
decisionRules.source: Two consecutive check-ins with an average home systolic BP 10 mmHg or more above goal despite confirmed adherence: provider review within 5 business days.

decisionRules.when: When any reading is in the severe range, then follow section 3.
decisionRules.source: Any reading in the severe range: follow section 3.

decisionRules.when: When angioedema occurs, then stop ACE inhibitors and ARBs.
decisionRules.source: Stop ACE inhibitors and ARBs if angioedema occurs.

decisionRules.when: When using an ACE inhibitor, do not combine it with an ARB.
decisionRules.then: Never combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB.
decisionRules.source: Never combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB.

titration.criteria: For Black patients without chronic kidney disease or albuminuria, start amlodipine 5 mg once daily or chlorthalidone 12.5 mg once daily instead.
titration.monitoring: Confirm adherence and home technique before every step. Allow 4 weeks between steps unless BP is in the severe range.

titration.criteria: Above goal on three agents including a diuretic at maximum tolerated doses (resistant hypertension), if potassium is below 4.5 mmol/L and eGFR is above 45 mL/min/1.73m2.
titration.monitoring: Refer to nephrology or a hypertension specialist.
titration.source: add spironolactone 25 mg once daily if potassium is below 4.5 mmol/L and eGFR is above 45 mL/min/1.73m2, and refer to nephrology or a hypertension specialist.
